summary: The grand bay entry is the Kinderlou Tower, a 54-ft former lookout now at Grand Bay WMA; a DNR notice dated 10/8/26 says the boardwalk to it is closed.

access.note: DNR notice posted 10/8/26: the boardwalk is closed until further notice. An undated alert on the same page gives gate hours for the boardwalk and lookout tower.

visit.trail_note: Reached by a half-mile boardwalk from the Grand Bay Wetland Education Center. The boardwalk is closed until further notice per the DNR notice posted 10/8/26.

corrections.why: The Georgia Encyclopedia calls the structure at Grand Bay the Kinderlou Tower. The list's grand bay label is its own, since the list says names for towers 73 and above are its creation (source 1).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The DNR page carries a dated notice (posted 10/8/26) that the boardwalk is closed until further notice, and an undated alert that the gate to the boardwalk and lookout tower is open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. The story follows the dated notice and flags the conflict.

notes_for_editor: Identity: the list's GA425 grand bay line carries the note Ron GA097-relocated, and GA097 is kinderlou (source 1). The 2012 essay and the Georgia Encyclopedia tie the Kinderlou Tower to the Grand Bay boardwalk. The move from Kinderlou Forest is inferred from those links; no source read dates or describes it. Suggest checking the GA097 kinderlou record as the likely original site; the list also has an 'old kinderlou' line (GA232) nearby. Access: the DNR page has a dated closure (10/8/26) and an undated gate alert; recheck with DNR before giving visit advice. The essay's climbing and GORP details are from 2012 and are not presented as current. Not used: a VisitValdosta Facebook post calling it a 'rebuilt fire tower' with a 2,600-foot walkway (social media, unverified), and a reader comment about the air base. Not the same structure as the NHLR Lowndes County Fire Tower (US 1474, GA 28, 100 ft, 1937); that entry is cited only to separate them. The list prints no elevation unit; 198 is read as feet, which matches the brief's 60.4 m. Budget: about eight page reads and two searches, over the six-read budget; the extra reads were the Georgia Encyclopedia and DNR pages, which carry the access evidence. The essay's 2012 date comes from its post URL (/2012/05/30/); the page text prints no year.
